answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may post jobs or claim rewards. When an agent proves a completed task, the contract releases its stake; if independent validators show the proof was forged or the task was never done, part of the bond is burned. A sybil attacker can forge many names, but cannot cheaply multiply their influence: every active identity ties up real capital, and any dishonest claim risks losing it. The voyage from fake accounts to profitable control thus demands a large, exposed stake, even across a karst of pseudonyms.
